findings.claim: The change modifies the decimal wire format in StandardClassLibraryFormatter by passing StandardFormat('F') to Utf8Formatter.TryFormat. This has nothing to do with REQ-2297, which is about attributes on generated code. With no explicit precision, the 'F' format is believed to use a fixed default number of fractional digits (2) instead of the round-trip 'G' form. If so, decimals such as 1.2345m would serialize as "1.23", silently losing data, and the bytes written for many decimal values would change.

receipt_plan.detail: Serialize 1.2345m, 0.000001m, 79228162514264337593543950335m and -1.5m with MessagePackSerializer using base-built and head-built MessagePack.dll and compare the bytes. Then deserialize the head bytes and assert each round-trips to the original value; expect 1.2345m to come back as 1.23m on head.

findings.claim: The requirement says all generated code gets the attribute. Every emitted attribute is wrapped in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`, so consumers compiling for netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework get no attribute at all. ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute exists on both targets (netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework 4.0+) and allows AttributeTargets.Class there, so the guard is unnecessary. It leaves a large class of projects without the requested behaviour.

receipt_plan.detail: Run ExcludeFromCodeCoverageDownlevelTargetsTests.GeneratedFormattersAreDecoratedWhenTargetingDownlevelFrameworks (NETSTANDARD2_0 and NETFRAMEWORK defined). It fails on head because no generated formatter carries the attribute. Also compile the generated code against netstandard2.0 reference assemblies with the #if removed to show it builds.

findings.claim: The README says the attribute is only emitted where it is available, 'not netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework'. This is factually wrong: the attribute is available on both targets. The docs therefore justify the coverage gap with an incorrect statement.

receipt_plan.detail: API docs for System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute list .NET Framework 4.0+ and .NET Standard 2.0 among the applies-to targets, contradicting README.md:1640.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Always emit, with no setting. [global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] is written into every generated type: int-key, string-key, enum and union formatters, the resolver, the composite resolver and their nested FormatterCache/GetFormatterHelper classes. There is no option to turn it off (the change additionally guards it with #if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK).

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Emit by default with an opt-out setting, which the requirement says 'would be fine to have too'. Add a bool such as ExcludeFromCodeCoverage (default true) to GeneratorOptions, read from an MSBuild property / analyzer config key (e.g. build_property.MessagePackExcludeFromCodeCoverage) or the GeneratedMessagePackResolver attribute. Wrap each attribute line in the .tt templates (Formatter, StringKeyFormatter, Enum, Union, Resolver, CompositeResolver) in `<# if (Options.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage) { #> ... <# } #>`, regenerate the .cs templates, and document the switch in README.
